audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Gragas levels 2, 3, first item and 2 items and calls level 1 and 6 even — but every why underneath describes Fiora winning. whys[0] 'You are the stronger level-1 duelist', whys[2] 'out-trades his poke even into his W', whys[4] 'R ... wins the all-in through his W', whys[5] 'Profane Hydra peaks your burst while his W ... never touches your Vital true damage'. Only whys[6] says coinflip. Packet levelChart: Fiora x6, then Skill.
audit.why: Body Slam is his only hard engage and it is an immobilising dash, so Riposte converts it into a stun — that alone gives Fiora the early duel. Barrel Roll costs 80 mana at every rank, which is unsustainable poke pre-item, and Drunken Rage's mitigation does nothing against Vital true damage. Only his ultimate displacement makes the 2-item window genuinely even.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 through First item -> Fiora; 2+ items -> Skill. Whole chart flipped as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly placed: 2-3 combo, level 6 Riposte-into-R, first item, and his Flash/Body Slam-into-R threat. Added Barrel Roll's 10s rank-1 cooldown and Body Slam's 14s so the windows are timed — the packet only counted one sequencing cue in the whole matchup.
audit.corrected: Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6s at 80 mana; Body Slam 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s; Explosive Cask 100/85/70s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly tells the player Gragas 'stands in the pool' from his Q to heal — whys[1] 'the mana to pool through it and heal back up', whys[3] 'his Q-pool mana', spikes[0] 'standing in the pool to heal it back', early 'poking Q and standing in the pool', wants.foe[1] 'sit in the pool to out-sustain'. Barrel Roll leaves no pool and no lingering zone.
audit.why: Kit text: 'Gragas rolls his cask to a location, which can be activated to explode or will explode on its own after 4 seconds ... Enemies struck by the blast have their Move Speed slowed.' It is a one-shot explosion. His actual sustain is Happy Hour (P) — 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill' — which is tied to casting, not to standing anywhere.
audit.corrected: Replaced every 'pool' reference with the real mechanics: an 80-mana Barrel Roll that self-detonates after 4 seconds, and Happy Hour healing on cast.

audit.why: The decisive interaction is stated and stated correctly: Body Slam is flagged hardCC and is a dash that stuns on collision, so Riposte blocks an immobilising effect and upgrades its stab to a stun. Explosive Cask is a knockback, not an immobilise, and spikes[3] correctly warns it 'can't be stunned out'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Drunken Rage's auto-attack reset is never mentioned, so the player has no tell for his burst.
audit.why: _missing/fiora.json flags autoreset-burst-tell for this matchup. The kit text gives the tell explicitly: 'Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second' before the empowered attack — a visible sip animation.
audit.corrected: Named the 1-second sip as the step-back cue in the mid text.

audit.why: _missing/fiora.json also flags needs-antiheal for Happy Hour. report[8] already prescribes early Executioner's Calling for this matchup, so the itemisation side is covered; the gap was only that the prose credited his sustain to the wrong ability.

edits.before: "Gragas wants to barrel-toss Q and Body Slam into you, but his E is the whole matchup — it is an immobilizing dash, so a clean Riposte turns it into a stun and a free Vital. Early he lacks the mana to keep poking Q and standing in the pool, so reach your level 2-3 combo: Lunge a Vital, then Bladework the guaranteed crit before he can heal it off. Don't walk into his Q at full mana, and never burn Riposte on a stray barrel — hold it for the Body Slam."
edits.after: "Gragas wants to roll barrels and Body Slam into you, but his E is the whole matchup — it is an immobilizing dash, so a clean Riposte turns it into a stun and a free Vital. Early he lacks the mana to keep rolling 80-mana barrels, so reach your level 2-3 combo: Lunge a Vital, then Bladework the guaranteed crit before Happy Hour heals it off. At 6 your R marks all four Vitals and the heal zone beats his Happy Hour sustain, though his own 6 is a Flash/Body Slam into R that flips you toward his jungler. Make him commit Body Slam first; parry it and the fight is already over."

notes: Biggest find in this matchup: five separate fields told the player Gragas heals by 'standing in the pool' from his Q. Barrel Roll is a single cask that detonates on activation or after 4 seconds — there is no pool. His sustain is Happy Hour (P), which heals on ability cast. All five corrected. Second: the level chart said Gragas or Skill for six of seven rows while every explanation under it described Fiora winning, and the packet chart agreed with the explanations. Minor inconsistency left alone: the content layer names Profane Hydra as the first-item spike while the full layer says Ravenous Hydra throughout — both are plausible Fiora builds, but the two layers should agree; flagging rather than picking one.
